_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the single input file x21-rd-input.json; no other repository file, search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: Bobbing for apples (APPLE) is the classic Halloween party game (HALLOWEEN); instant and clean on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but very satisfying; lines are accurate.

hints.reason: Mary Poppins's bottomless carpet bag (BAG) and her flying umbrella (UMBRELLA) are her two signature props.

pairs.pair_note: Strong. Note POPPINS is also the hint for p_umbrella__wind; both pairs contain UMBRELLA, so never serve both on one board.

hints.reason: Peppermint bark (BARK) is a staple holiday candy, and peppermint and candy canes are classic Christmas flavors (CHRISTMAS); the bark-as-candy sense is a nice misdirect from tree or dog bark.

pairs.pair_note: Good misdirection on BARK; lines accurate.

hints.reason: Basketball is played on a court (BASKETBALL) and malls have food courts (FOOD); a clear, familiar double use.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and easy.

hints.reason: Washington is on the one-dollar bill (BILL) and was the first U.S. president (FIRST); FIRST is an abstract target and this makes it click.

pairs.pair_note: Good use of an abstract target; facts correct.

hints.reason: A plank is a board (BOARD) and the plank is a staple core exercise (GYM); synonym on one side but a real second sense on the other.

pairs.pair_note: Solid double meaning.

hints.reason: Bowser is the recurring final boss of Mario games (BOSS) who kidnaps Princess Peach (PRINCESS).

pairs.pair_note: Familiar video-game reference; lines hedge correctly with 'many' and 'often'.

hints.reason: Pandora's box from Greek myth (BOX) and the Pandora music streaming service (MUSIC); myth-to-brand jump gives a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the BOX line rightly says 'popular telling' (the original was a jar).

hints.reason: A scarab is a beetle (BUG) and the scarab was a sacred symbol of ancient Egypt (EGYPT).

pairs.pair_note: Fair and accurate; Khepri detail is correct.

hints.reason: Ms. Frizzle drives the Magic School Bus, linking BUS and MAGIC through one beloved kids' character.

pairs.pair_note: Both targets come from the title, but the character name makes it a satisfying recall rather than a bare phrase.

hints.reason: Candy cane (CANDY) and a cane as a walking stick (STICK); clear on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, honest double meaning.

hints.reason: A manual car / owner's manual (CAR) and 'driving stick' meaning driving a manual (STICK); the stick-shift sense is a nice turn on STICK.

pairs.pair_note: Good. STICK also appears in p_candy__stick; avoid serving both pairs on one board.

hints.reason: A cat's nine lives (CAT) and being on cloud nine (CLOUD); two instantly familiar idioms that pair nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but both phrases are instant and the number hint is a pleasing surprise.

hints.reason: Swiss cheese (CHEESE) and the Swiss Army knife multi-tool (TOOL); both are household names.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that is instantly familiar; the multi-tool link to TOOL needs one small step, which is fine.

hints.reason: The pope leads the Catholic Church (CHURCH) and white smoke from the Sistine Chapel announces a new pope (SMOKE).

pairs.pair_note: Lovely aha on SMOKE; facts accurate.

hints.reason: Tide laundry detergent (CLEAN) and the Moon's gravity driving ocean tides (MOON); brand-to-science jump is a real 'oh, nice'.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: The fine print of a contract (CONTRACT), with fine meaning tiny or thin as in fine print or fine sand (SMALL); the SMALL side leans on the same phrase but still reads naturally.

pairs.pair_note: SMALL is the softer side; 'fine print' = 'small print' carries it. Lines accurate.

hints.reason: Peter Pan's clock-swallowing crocodile, Tick-Tock (CROCODILE), and the tick-tock of a watch (WATCH); hyphenated form is allowed.

pairs.pair_note: Delightful; the CROCODILE side gives the aha, WATCH is the easy anchor.

hints.reason: The shuffle dance step (DANCE) and shuffling a deck of cards (DECK).

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning.

hints.reason: Labor Day (DAY) and labor as a synonym for work (WORK); the holiday gives the second connection.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; synonym on WORK is fine because Labor Day ties DAY honestly.

hints.reason: Cartoon devils carry pitchforks (DEVIL) and angry mobs carry torches and pitchforks (TORCH).

pairs.pair_note: Good; DEVIL line rightly hedges with 'often drawn'.

hints.reason: A china doll (DOLL) and china as another name for porcelain (PORCELAIN).
hints.fix: DOLL line: "A china doll is a doll whose head is made of glazed porcelain."

pairs.pair_note: Route is sound; small precision fix because classic china dolls usually have only a porcelain head (and often limbs) on a cloth body.

hints.reason: "Hotel California" (HOTEL) is the Eagles' signature song (EAGLE); classic rock that most U.S. players know.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-like on HOTEL but the band link makes it a satisfying recall; 1976 date correct.

hints.reason: The Munsters is a sitcom about a family (FAMILY) of monsters led by a Frankenstein's-monster dad (MONSTER), with a Munster/monster sound echo.

pairs.pair_note: 1960s show but widely known through reruns and the 2022 film; plural form is the show title, not a target plural.

hints.reason: Piranhas are sharp-toothed fish (FISH) and Piranha Plants bite Mario from pipes (PLANT).

pairs.pair_note: Great real-world/game crossover; PLANT also appears in p_plant__thumb, so avoid one board with both.

hints.reason: Bigfoot (FOOT) plus the famous giant floor-piano scene in the film Big (PIANO); the PIANO side needs the film recall but clicks hard once seen.
hints.fix: PIANO line: "In the 1988 film Big, Tom Hanks dances out a tune on a giant floor piano in a toy store."

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: BIG is broad, so PIANO is not obvious during play, but the FAO Schwarz scene is iconic; the PIANO line's parenthetical is clumsy, hence the fix.

hints.reason: Bastille Day is France's national holiday (FRANCE) commemorating the storming of the Bastille (STORM); the STORM-as-attack sense is a nice turn.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; dates accurate.

hints.reason: A carol is a Christmas song (SONG) and A Christmas Carol is a ghost story (GHOST).

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect link; 'three ghosts' plus Marley is the common telling and the line covers Marley.

hints.reason: The god Pan is half goat (GOAT) and pan pipes are named for him (PIPE).

pairs.pair_note: Fair myth link; pan pipes make PIPE accessible even if Pan's goat legs are less known.

hints.reason: A hammer drives a nail (HAMMER) and you hit the nail on the head (HEAD).

pairs.pair_note: Idiom ties all three words together neatly.

hints.reason: A cricket is a chirping insect (INSECT) and cricket is a bat-and-ball sport (SPORT).

pairs.pair_note: Classic double meaning; U.S. players know the sport by name even if they don't follow it.

hints.reason: King Kong (KING) lives on Skull Island (SKULL), well known from the 2017 film Kong: Skull Island.

pairs.pair_note: Skull Island is moderately known; the 2017 film title makes it fair.

hints.reason: You write a letter with a pen (LETTER) and the pen is mightier than the sword (SWORD).

pairs.pair_note: LETTER side is generic but true; the proverb carries the pair.

hints.reason: Sets make up a tennis match, as in game, set, match (MATCH), and you set the table (TABLE).

pairs.pair_note: Simple double meaning; SET is broad but both routes are honest.

hints.reason: Psychics claim to read minds (MIND) and read palms (PALM).

pairs.pair_note: READER (mind reader, palm reader) is an equally good alternative; PSYCHIC is fine as is.

hints.reason: Netflix's all-at-once releases invite binge-watching (NETFLIX), and you binge a show (SHOW).

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate; 'often' hedge is correct.

hints.reason: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa (PAINTING) and Leonardo is a shelled Ninja Turtle (SHELL).

pairs.pair_note: Classic artist/turtle double; very satisfying.

hints.reason: A green thumb (THUMB) is a knack for growing plants, which are mostly green (PLANT).

pairs.pair_note: The idiom itself is about plants, so both sides connect through meaning, not just the phrase.

hints.reason: Sonic the Hedgehog collects rings (RING) and sonic means relating to sound (SOUND).

pairs.pair_note: Excellent game-plus-vocabulary double.

hints.reason: Scuba diving (SCUBA DIVER) and skydiving (SKY) both work, but DIVING is just an inflected form of the target word DIVER, so it gives the answer away rather than clueing it.

pairs.pair_note: Not a literal substring, but the shared root DIV- breaks the spirit of the no-target-in-hint rule; I found no clearly better one-word hint for this pair.

hints.reason: Skin has pores (SKIN) and sponges are full of pores, Porifera meaning pore-bearing (SPONGE).

pairs.pair_note: Accurate science; Porifera detail is a nice bonus.

hints.reason: David Beckham the soccer star (SOCCER) and Victoria Beckham, Posh Spice (SPICE); the married-couple link is a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; SPICE-as-Spice-Girls is a lovely misdirect.

hints.reason: Summer heat (SUMMER) and a heat wave (WAVE).

pairs.pair_note: Easy phrase-join, but meaningful on both sides.

hints.reason: Mary Poppins flies with her umbrella (UMBRELLA) and blows in on the east wind (WIND); the wind detail is less universally recalled but true in book and film.

pairs.pair_note: WIND is the weaker side; same hint as p_bag__umbrella, and both pairs contain UMBRELLA, so never serve both on one board.
